text:
jonathan_support: FYI customer acme-prod opened an escalation: streaming responses p99 TTFB spiked ~48h ago. non-streaming endpoints show normal latency. customer sees p99 TTFB ~2.5-3s (was ~150-300ms). sample request IDs: req_98765, req_98766. Link to logs: https://internal.log/acme-prod/req_98765 :eyes:

maria_ops: which region/model/transport? SSE or h2? tenant id?

jonathan_support: region=us-west1, model=gpt-4o-mini (open variant), transport=SSE (streaming). tenant=acme-prod. They also provided a small repro in their app + curl.

devon_eng: Can you paste the exact curl they used? we should try to reproduce from our CLI (both SSE and non-streaming) before chasing infra.

jonathan_support: here's the curl they used (they said it reliably shows long TTFB):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","prompt":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```
They also tried non-streaming endpoint and got <300ms.

jonathan_support: pasted a snippet from edge-proxy logs around req_98765: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:14:07Z] req=98765 buf_len=0 -> buffering first chunk
[2026-03-15T12:14:07Z] req=98765 holdback_timer_ms=500
[2026-03-15T12:14:09Z] req=98765 chunk_emit reason=holdback_expired elapsed_ms=2650
[2026-03-15T12:14:09Z] req=98765 sent bytes=420
```
Notice holdback_timer_ms=500 but elapsed_ms shows 2650 (something coalesced).

devon_eng: Interesting — edge emitted by holdback expiry but elapsed much higher. Could be connection scheduling/backpressure upstream or coalescing queue starvation. Can we repro in lab by forcing heavy muxing + keepalive?

max_infra: Quick data point: we rolled edge-proxy v3.2.1 two days ago; it includes a change that raised default COALESCE_WINDOW_MS from 50 -> 500 to reduce small-chunk overhead for high throughput. rollout was gradual across regions. I can point to the PR: https://git.internal/edge/PR-842

lisa_prod: That aligns with timeline. For streaming small responses, increasing coalescing window will inflate TTFB. Customer appears to have many short initial chunks; the bigger window delays first byte.

devon_eng: Agreed. Immediate mitigations:
- tenant override: set COALESCE_WINDOW_MS=50 for tenant acme-prod (should drop TTFB back down)
- if tenant prefers, enable non-streaming fallback for their requests while we triage
- roll a canary revert of the default to 50ms in us-west1 edges serving acme-prod

jonathan_support: Can we do tenant override now? customer asked for quick fix; they'll accept temporary non-streaming fallback too.

max_infra: I can apply tenant override via config-store. command: 
```
kubectl -n config-store exec -it config-store-0 -- /bin/sh -c \
  'rdctl tenancy update acme-prod --set "edge.coalesce_ms=50"'
```
I'll scope to us-west1 first.

maria_ops: I'll coordinate with max. I'll also run a quick Datadog query to watch TTFB p99 for streaming in us-west1: 
```
avg:trace.redwood.request.latency{transport:stream,region:us-west1}.percentile(99)
```
Can we add a temporary dashboard panel for acme-prod?

lisa_prod: Yes please. Also update docs to note that COALESCE_WINDOW_MS affects initial TTFB vs throughput tradeoff. We'll make it togglable per-tenant from Console.

devon_eng: Longer term: implement adaptive heuristic instead of fixed window. Use early-detection: if expected token output < X bytes or model indicates short response, flush aggressively (<=50ms). If throughput > threshold, increase coalesce. Also add telemetry: "initial_chunk_size_histogram" and correlate with p99 TTFB.

jonathan_support: Customer ok with tenant override. They'll validate in ~15m. I'll reply to their ticket with repro steps we used and ask them to confirm streaming p99 after override. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy edge-config change for acme-prod started by max_infra. CI ✅, canary nodes: edge-usw1-0..3.

max_infra: override pushed to canary nodes (edge-usw1-0..3) at 12:47 PST. Monitoring now.

maria_ops: initial numbers: before override p99 streaming TTFB ~2.6s; after override on canary nodes p99 ~180ms for those nodes. Observed 60% of acme traffic hit canary nodes; overall p99 dropped to ~1.1s so far.

jonathan_support: customer confirms improved latency in their app when routed to canary. They want full rollback or tenant override for the rest.

max_infra: planning to roll override to all us-west1 edges in next 10m, then rest of regions. Will monitor error rates.

devon_eng: action items (owners):
- max_infra: roll tenant override to all regions (ETA 30m)
- lisa_prod: add Console toggle + docs (ETA 2d)
- devon_eng: implement adaptive heuristic + tests (ETA 2w)
- maria_ops: dashboard + SLO alert temporarily sensitive to streaming TTFB (ETA 1h)
- jonathan_support: communicate with customer and close ticket if green (ETA now)

jonathan_support: will update customer and close once global metrics stable. thanks team.

maria_ops: I'll keep watch for regressions and create postmortem note if needed.

sre-bot: canary->global rollout of override complete at 13:28 PST.

max_infra: override applied globally for acme-prod. Confirmed no increase in 5xx.

lisa_prod: opened a small feature request to add per-tenant streaming-flush override in Console: FE-901.

devon_eng: I'll open a follow-up issue to revert v3.2.1 default and bake adaptive heuristic: INFRA-432.

jonathan_support: closing thread after customer acknowledges improvement. Summary saved to ticket. :white_check_mark:
